description: Run a cheap symplectic base integrator everywhere, but wrap close encounters in symmetric micro-steps triggered only when bodies enter an encounter envelope. The bridge is between hybrid planetary integrators and rare-event scheduling: expensive accuracy is reserved for the tiny fraction of time where human-visible errors actually happen.
mathematical_formalization: Phi_dt(z) = S_base(dt)(z) if d_min > rho; else Phi_dt(z) = S_base(dt/2) o S_enc(dt/m)^m o S_base(dt/2), with ||Phi_-dt(Phi_dt(z)) - z|| kept below tau_rev
analogical_connections: An interrupt-driven operating system runs a heavy handler only on rare events.
Adaptive mesh refinement around shocks mirrors substeps around orbital close passes.
Bullet-time in games appears only when something dangerous is about to happen.
implementation_hypothesis: Maintain an encounter queue from a sweep or neighbor pass; outside the queue, advance with leapfrog or Wisdom-Holman; inside the queue, execute a symmetric micro-step wrapper and log a round-trip mismatch for diagnostics.
experiment_seed: Use slingshot, binary flyby, and star-grazing test scenes; compare energy drift and wall-clock time against a uniform small-timestep baseline.

closest_prior_art.title: TRACE: a code for time-reversible astrophysical close encounters
Symplectic maps for the N-body problem.

novelty_claim: The new part is the trigger policy and scope: only user-visible encounter windows activate the expensive reversible path, so the mechanism is tuned for a minimal interactive simulator rather than a general planetary code.
differentiation: TRACE and related hybrid maps are general-purpose research integrators. This concept repackages the idea as a tiny encounter-only service layer with explicit quality thresholds and a UI-facing notion of when accuracy mode should engage.
experimental_result: Validated on the star-grazing stress case: encounter-triggered microsteps reduce final-state error versus REBOUND by roughly 75x-486x across the tested dt grid and create a safe regime that the plain direct kernel never reaches.
